standard_prerequisites.name: The cap with the first Chern class of an invertible sheaf, defined through the divisor associated to a section
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, the construction of the cap with $c_1$ for invertible sheaves (used at proof lines 4344-4346 and 4349)
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the definition the additivity statement is compared against, and it is what makes the vanishing for $\mathcal{O}_X$ follow from the behaviour of the constant section.

core_obligations: Reduce the additivity assertion to the corresponding additivity for the divisors attached to the invertible sheaves, using the definitions (proof lines 4344-4346).

For the trivial sheaf, take the section $1 \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ and note that it restricts to an everywhere nonzero section on every integral closed subscheme $W \subset X$ (proof lines 4346-4349).
Conclude $c_1(\mathcal{O}_X) \cap [W] = 0$ for each such $W$, and hence $c_1(\mathcal{O}_X) \cap \alpha = 0$ for all $\alpha$ (proof line 4349).
proof_roadmap: Additivity from the divisor statement and the definitions (proof lines 4344-4346).
The constant section on an integral subscheme (proof lines 4346-4348).
Vanishing of the cap with the trivial sheaf (proof line 4349).
difficulty_reason: The lemma records the two structural properties of the cap with a first Chern class: additivity in the tensor product of two invertible sheaves and vanishing for the trivial sheaf (statement lines 4329-4341). The additivity is read off from the known additivity of the divisor construction, while the vanishing is proved by exhibiting the constant section, which is everywhere nonzero on each integral closed subscheme. The argument on the constant section is the substance, so the claim is H2.
